title: ACME Healthcare - POC scoping: quality eval plan
summary: POC scoping to align on success criteria for a quality evaluation plan: define golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring approach, workload sizing and timeline. Agreed next steps: Redwood to deliver a detailed eval plan, sample benchmarks and pricing; ACME to share sample data and acceptance criteria by next Tuesday.
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-05-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 60 min
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (ACME PM), Dr. Naveen Patel (ACME CTO), Aisha Brown (ACME Data Eng)

[00:00] Samantha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side, I'm Samantha, AE for Redwood; Diego is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Laura: Hi all, Laura here, PM for the patient intake project. We're mainly focused on triage summaries and question/answer for patient forms.
[00:15] Diego: Great, could you frame the main success criteria up front? i.e., what does a successful pilot look like for ACME?
[00:23] Laura: Sure. Top line: high factual accuracy on discharge summaries (>95% on key fields), hallucination rate under 2% on clinician prompts, output format strictness (JSON with specified schema), and latency under 800ms P95 for a single-threaded call. Also cost target we'll discuss.
[00:40] Dr. Patel: Security is non-negotiable — we need VPC/private deployment and audit logs for every inference. SOC2 docs would help.
[00:48] Samantha: Yep, we can provide SOC2 and our security pack. For the POC we typically propose a dedicated instance or Redwood Private depending on the data flow.
[00:56] Aisha: Quick note on data: we can share redacted sample forms (around 10k rows) and a golden set of 200 examples we use as reference.
[01:05] Diego: Perfect. On the quality eval plan: we'll build three pillars — golden prompts (the canonical inputs and expected outputs), regression suites (older prompts + new prompts to detect regressions), and hallucination/format checks (entity-level checks and schema conformance).
[01:25] Laura: Can you unpack the scoring approach? How do you balance format conformance vs. semantic correctness?
[01:31] Diego: Sure. Practical approach: layered scoring. First, format penalty — if response doesn't parse to the JSON schema it's automatically failed or gets big penalty. Second, entity extraction F1 for key fields (like patient name obfuscated, diagnosis codes). Third, hallucination score which is a binary check for invented facts against the input/context; we weight hallucination highest in the final composite score. So final score = 0.5 * entity-F1 + 0.3 * format-pass + 0.2 * (1 - hallucination-rate). We can tweak weights per ACME priorities.
[02:05] Dr. Patel: That sounds reasonable. What's your methodology for hallucination detection? Automated checks? Human review?
[02:12] Diego: We combine deterministic checks (e.g., if output references a medication not present in input it's flagged) and spot human annotations for edge cases. For the POC we'll run automated checks and sample 10% for manual review to calibrate thresholds.
[02:28] Laura: What about regression tests — do you keep previous model outputs?
[02:33] Samantha: Yes, we snapshot baseline model outputs and run diffing. For the POC we recommend establishing a baseline run (your current in-house model or an open model) and then compare Redwood-run outputs to detect regressions or improvements.
[02:46] Aisha: Workload sizing — our expected volumes are ~3k calls/day during pilot, peaking at 10k/day for burst windows, average token length ~450 tokens.
[02:55] Diego: Thanks, that helps. For that workload we suggest starting on a single dedicated GPU pool (A100 or comparable). We'll run throughput benchmarks; expected throughput should comfortably meet your latency target with batching disabled for low-latency calls.
[03:10] Laura: Benchmarks — can you run both quality and performance benchmarks?
[03:13] Diego: Yes. We'll produce: 1) quality benchmark report (golden set scoring, regression diffs, hallucination stats), 2) latency/throughput benchmarks (P95/P99 for given batch sizes), and 3) cost estimates per 1M tokens for the chosen config.
[03:29] Laura: Timeline? We want a 6-week pilot ideally.
[03:32] Samantha: Typical POC timeline: Week 0 - kickoff and data exchange; Week 1 - baseline runs and golden prompt curation; Week 2 - implement eval harness + automated checks; Week 3 - run benchmarks and iterate; Week 4 - manual review and threshold tuning; Week 5 - stability testing and integration; Week 6 - final report and decision. We can compress to 4 weeks if ACME provides data and acceptance criteria immediately.
[03:57] Dr. Patel: Dependencies from our side: dataset (redacted), SSO access for console, network for VPC peering, and a list of stakeholders.
[04:06] Samantha: Noted. On golden prompts: please share the 200 canonical examples. We'll expand them to cover edge cases (abbreviations, typos, incomplete forms) and craft adversarial prompts to stress hallucination.
[04:21] Laura: For scoring thresholds — is 95% entity F1 realistic?
[04:25] Diego: For structured fields (codes, dates, enums) yes, for free-text diagnosis maybe lower. We recommend per-field targets: 98% for enums/dates, 90%+ for free-text key phrases.
[04:36] Aisha: Formatting enforcement — can you auto-correct minor issues or must it be exact?
[04:40] Diego: For POC we treat format strictness as pass/fail; we can add a soft-correction pipeline but that adds latency and complexity. We can prototype both.
[04:51] Laura: How will you surface hallucination examples? We want a dashboard with sampled false positives.
[04:55] Samantha: Redwood Console will show per-route hallucination rate, sample failing responses, and ability to drill into tokens. We'll include screenshots in the POC report.
[05:04] Dr. Patel: Security again, encryption at rest and in-transit plus KMS — you support customer-managed keys?
[05:10] Samantha: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM. For the pilot we can use our sandbox KMS or integrate yours if timeline allows.
[05:20] Laura: Anything else around acceptance criteria?
[05:23] Diego: We'll formalize an acceptance matrix: quality thresholds per field, P95 latency target, max hallucination rate, availability SLA for the pilot env. If those are met, the pilot is a success.
[05:35] Laura: Ok, sounds good. Pricing and security docs?
[05:38] Samantha: I'll share pricing tiers for the pilot/dedicated and the security package. Expect an email by Friday.
[05:44] Aisha: We'll share the redacted dataset and the golden 200 examples by Monday.
[05:49] Samantha: Great. Quick recap of next steps...
[05:52] [crosstalk]
[05:54] Samantha: Action items: Redwood to send eval plan, benchmark template, security pack, and pilot pricing. ACME to send data, golden prompts, and stakeholder list.
[06:04] Laura: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the thread.
[06:07] Samantha: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings (K-V cache noted as K-V cash in one spot), occasional filler words.

End of transcript.
